AUTHOR: Veiga
TITLE: Autonomous temporal pseudo-labeling for fish detection
REGION: Algarve coast, Portugal (CCMAR BRUV footage, 'diverse habitats'); baseline from OzFish (Australia)
SPECIES: Single class 'fish' (Portuguese Atlantic fauna; OzFish Australian fauna for baseline)
DATA: OzFish (1,753 annotated frames, 80/15/5) + CCMAR negative frames; 21 unlabelled CCMAR BRUV videos (695 min) pseudo-labelled (up to 35,510 training images incl. negatives); 383 biologist-annotated unseen test images
V_EV: Sec. 7: 'multiple underwater environments and conditions, including obscured scenarios with the suspension of sand, were used and tested' — qualitative only, no stratified results
D2: OzFish 80/15/5 (train/val/test); CCMAR pseudo-labelled frames for training; 383 'unseen' biologist-annotated images for test
D_EV: no statement found on split unit (Sec. 4: 'A collection of 383 unseen images from different areas were annotated by a marine biologist'; Sec. 5.3: temporal threshold tt = 20 s 'to prevent over-similar images from the same sequences')
R_EV: Table 2 / Sec. 6: OzFish-trained YOLOv4 'evaluated on the unseen image collection annotated by a CCMAR marine biologist'; 'mAP50 rising 25.45% from 48.60% to 74.05%'
C_EV: Table 2 note: 'Confidence threshold at 50% on the left, and 10% on the right'; Sec. 6: 'the direct relation between precision and recall with the variation of the confidence threshold'
E_EV: Abstract: 'achieved a mean average precision of 93.11% on our own data, and 73.61% on unseen data' — only mAP/IoU/precision/recall reported
ARCH: YOLOv4 (MS-COCO pre-trained, single 'fish' class, 608x608; also YOLOv4-tiny, YOLOv4-tiny-3l) with self-supervised temporal pseudo-labelling loop using a Euclidean-distance tracker and progressive blur of undetected areas
METR: mAP50 93.11% / mAP75 74.70% on generated CCMAR data; mAP50 74.05% / mAP75 43.40% on 383 biologist-annotated unseen images; precision/recall at conf 0.5 and 0.1
NOTE: D1 ambiguous: the 383 test images are described as 'unseen' and 'from different areas/locations' but the paper does not state whether they come from videos or sites excluded from the pseudo-labelling pool (coded NR; verifier may consider 사이트/서식지, which would make D_ALL = Y). D3 = Y for the 20-s temporal threshold filtering near-duplicate frames. R1 = Y because the OzFish-trained baseline (Australia) is evaluated on Portuguese CCMAR footage (different region, species, camera, conditions) with results reported separately in Table 2; the final CCMAR-trained model itself is tested in-domain. NIMG = 35,510 training images (half negative samples) for the best model; 383 ground-truth test images. Table 1 metrics on generated data are evaluated against pseudo-labels, not human ground truth. Data availability 'Not applicable'; CCMAR dataset promised in a future paper. Abstract says 73.61% mAP on unseen data while Table 2 gives 74.05%.
